name: Automath
typeSystem: The first dependently typed system: mathematical statements are encoded as types and proofs as terms inhabiting them (following the Curry-Howard correspondence), checked purely by type checking rather than by dedicated inference rules.
runtime: Automath texts were checked by small, standalone type-checking programs (written in languages such as ALGOL 60/BCPL of the era); there was no interactive proof state or tactic language, just batch verification of a fully written-out proof term.

runtimes.name: Batch type checker
runtimes.role: Reads a complete Automath text and either accepts every definition and proof term as well-typed or reports a type error.

compilers.name: Automath checking programs
compilers.role: De Bruijn-era implementations that checked complete texts written in Automath dialects such as AUT-68 and AUT-QE.

concurrencyModel: N/A (batch proof-checking language, no runtime execution model)

codeExample.caption: Authentic AUT-QE-style declaration of a primitive binary relation
